before: Node, part, relationship, content type, binary, namespace, attribute, binding, and paragraph text records were stored under root maps with names such as docx-package-attributes-v1, and each node record stored its child array under the field children. Yjs writes the root name into every entry of a root-level map, so these names made up 5% to 18% of a room. The room of a 75 KB document was 4.2 MiB.
after: These records are stored under root maps named dx:n, dx:p, dx:r, dx:o, dx:d, dx:x, dx:s, dx:a, dx:b, dx:td, dx:tc, and dx:tm, and each node record stores its child array under the field c. The same document makes a room of 3.5 MiB. The format fields stay in docx-package-meta-v1, so every release still reads the format of any room and refuses one of another format before it reads records. Shared blobs and seed records keep their names.
reason: A replica of shared schema version 5 looks for its records under the long names, so it reads a version 6 room as empty, and the reverse. sharedSchemaVersion increases to 6 (format docx-collaboration:1.6.6.1), so the two versions refuse to share a room before any update applies. An upgrade seeds the room again from its DOCX export, as for every format change, and reads nothing from the earlier roots.

supersedesTests.reason: Format 1.5.6.1 ships combined with this change as format 1.6.6.1, so the test checks the upgrade to the combined format.
